fields.AN_Notes: Bias_Axes: the work compares female and male participants on concepts test, AI literacy and AI empowerment; study background and programming experience are non-social variables and are not coded as axes. Harm_Types None: the work establishes no harm mechanism of an AI system for its own object; gender stereotypes are offered as cited explanation of the empowerment gap. Mitigation: the intervention is a 7-hour AI literacy course (training) whose reported result is that the pre-course gender gap in self-perceived AI empowerment no longer existed after the course (Table 5); the course addresses a gender gap in AI learning, not algorithmic bias, so Organisational_Process and Evaluated are limited to this training intervention and its own pre-post result. AN_Task None: AI is the learning content of the course, the work describes no professional task performed with AI. Gender is used as two categories ('both genders'), no definition. Theory_Reference No: self-efficacy (Bandura) and programming empowerment frame empowerment, not gender or bias.

fields.AN_Notes: Prompts (sentence completions, story prompts) serve as bias probes; no named technique. Bias_Axes: Gender and Age from the word-embedding association test (Study 1, 'age and pleasantness'), Race_Ethnicity and Sexual_Orientation_Identity from the regard study (Study 2, subjects varying by gender and race, gay subjects), Language_Culture from British and Zulu subjects named as cultural backgrounds (Study 3), Nationality_Migration from nationality-combined story prompts (Global North/South). Intersectional is coded because Study 3 reports occupations that differ by the combination of gender and culture (Zulu women domestic and service roles, British women other stereotyped roles, Zulu men gardener or security guard); the work itself lists 'Need for Intersectional Analysis' as a limitation, which the AI Agent Review may weigh. Harm_Types: Stereotyping from Studies 1 and 3, Derogatory_Language from sexist, misogynistic and anti-gay completions. Repetitiveness of text for women and local groups is a difference in output diversity and style and is not coded as Disparate_Performance. Mitigation: dataset curation and augmentation (Pre_Processing), adversarial training and RLHF (In_Training), audits, oversight, impact assessments and diverse teams (Organisational_Process). Status Evaluated rests only on the reported comparison that the RLHF-tuned ChatGPT produced positive or neutral content in over 80% of cases while non-RLHF models did not; this is a cross-model comparison, not a controlled test, and all other recommendations remain Proposed. Gender is analysed as woman/man and girl/boy; the statement about 'the complexity of human gender identities' is a recommendation the analysis does not follow. Theory_Reference No: the implicit association test is used as method, no theory frames gender or bias.

fields.AN_Notes: Bias_Axes: economically disadvantaged groups are the work's own worked example of data imbalance in social services; 'minority groups' and 'marginalized groups' stay unspecified and are not coded. Harm_Types: Disparate_Performance from systems that cannot accurately gauge the needs of underrepresented groups; Direct_Discrimination from the argued denial of services and resources 'based on their inherent characteristics', read as a decision that changes with the group attribute itself (the work does not itself classify direct versus indirect). The single sentence that biases 'threaten to perpetuate stereotypes' is asserted without a mechanism and is not coded as Stereotyping. Mitigation: diverse and representative datasets (Pre_Processing); transparency, oversight, training of social workers and legal regulation (Organisational_Process); all proposed. AN_Task: the work names risk assessment algorithms and the delegation of critical decisions to AI in social work. Bias is explained through data imbalance and feedback loops without a determining sentence.

fields.AN_Notes: Online survey comparing women and men on perceived opportunities, self-assessed competence, interest and trust regarding AI in the world of work. Bias_Axes Gender only; the age correlation with trust is a side finding not framed as disadvantage and is not coded. Harm_Types None: the discrimination cases in section 2.3.2 (Facebook STEM ads, Amazon recruiting, voice and face recognition) are cited from other work and the work's own results concern perception, not an AI harm mechanism. Mitigation: more women and diverse persons in AI development, AI competence and sensitisation, ethical requirements and the AIF360 toolkit are recommended (Organisational_Process, Proposed); representative datasets appear only in cited background. AN_Task None: the survey asks about attitudes towards AI in workplace functions such as recruitment and customer service but describes or proposes no task performed with AI. Gender_Understanding: the analysis compares two categories and removes four persons who chose 'divers' (Binary_Categorical), while the definition states gender as social gender shaped by history and social change and the hypotheses are derived from socialisation and role expectations (Social_Construct); the pairing is a recorded open question. Theory: gender role concept and role theory frame the hypotheses on gender differences.
